figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. (A) Schematic diagram showing the mode of action of peptidyl-nucleotide antibiotics. (B) Organization of the biosynthetic gene cluster
(top) and the key steps in the biosynthetic pathway of E. coli microcin C (bottom). MccAEco, precursor peptide; MccBEco, adenylyltransferase;
MccCEco, major facilitator superfamily export pump; MccDEco, aminocarboxypropyl (ACP) transferase; MccE1Eco domain, decarboxylase; MccE2Eco
domain, N-acetyltransferase; MccFEco, L,D-peptidase. MccE2Eco and MccFEco are responsible for the immunity function. YejABEF and PDF are the
cellular oligopeptide transporter and peptide deformylase, respectively. The isoasparaginyl-adenylate warhead of microcin C is designated as pMcC.
R stands for the N-terminal part of MccAEco, MRTGNA. Eco-McC, adenylated MccAEco; Eco-McCacp, adenylated MccAEco decorated with 3-amino-
3-carboxypropyl group; Eco-McCap, mature aminopropylated peptidyl-adenylate E. coli, MTA, 5′-methylthioadenosine.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. B. subtilis MG27 mcc gene cluster (mccBsu) and its products. (A) Architecture of the mccBsu cluster and the sequence of the predicted
precursor peptide MccABsu. Arrows representing genes are colored according to their functional annotations: mccCBsu, MFS transporter; mccBBsu,
nucleotidyltransferase; mccM1Bsu and mccM2Bsu, SAM-dependent enzymes; mccABsu, precursor peptide; mccE2, acetyltransferase. (B) MALDI-TOF
MS analyses of the spent media of the control B. subtilis 168 carrying empty pHT01 control vector (upper panel) or pHT-mccCM1BAM2Bsu
plasmid (lower panel). [M + H]+ ions related to the mccCM1BAM2Bsu expression products are labeled in red. (C) MALDI-TOF/TOF MS analysis
of the [M + H]+ = 1222.5. [M + H]+ product ions at m/z = 250 and m/z = 779 correspond to adenosine and the FDGPVMiN peptide,
respectively. The [M + H]+ product ions at m/z = 1087 and 973 correspond to the modified peptides that lost adenosine and adenine moieties,
respectively. The difference in 194 Da between [M + H]+ = 779 and [M + H]+ = 973 matches the phosphate residue (80 Da) bearing an unknown
114-Da modification designated with ″X″. The product ion [M + H]+ = 1108, corresponding to the mature peptide that lost the 114-Da unknown
modification, is complemented by [M + H]+ = 115.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. MccM1Bsu and MccM2Bsu catalyze the sequential addition of two aminopropyl groups on peptidyl-adenylate. (A) High-resolution mass-
spectrum and chemical formula of Bsu-McC. (B) Two-dimensional 1H−13C HSQC (blue) and HSQC-Dipsi (red) NMR spectra show the
assignment of the two aminopropyl groups that decorate the phosphate group of the AMP moiety. (C) The overlay of two J-resolved spectra with
(red) or without (magenta) recoupling of the 1H and 31P coupling constants identifies those protons with a direct scalar coupling constant to the
31P. Dashed arrows point to the chemical shift values of the 31P coupled ribose CH2 protons and the α proton of the proximal propyl group, for
which the two spectra are different. (D) Proposed chemical structure of Bsu-McC with numbering of the tandem aminopropyl atoms. R stands for
the peptidyl moiety FDGPVM. (E) MALDI-TOF MS analysis of spent media (left) and cell content (right) of B. subtilis 168 harboring plasmids
with mccBsu cluster variants and the control vector. For detailed spectra analysis, see the text.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. MccM1Bsu and MccM2Bsu use decarboxylated SAM as a substrate for aminopropylation. (A) MALDI-TOF MS analysis of in vitro
aminopropylation reactions. MccM1Bsu transfers the aminopropyl group from dcSAM to peptidyl-adenylate MccABsu-AMP ([M + H]+ = 2856.6).
MccM2Bsu converts aminopropylated peptidyl-adenylate ([M + H]+ = 2913.6) into a tandem aminopropylated form ([M + H]+ = 2970.7) using
dcSAM. (B) SpeDBsu activity is required for the maturation of Bsu-McC in vivo. MALDI-TOF MS analysis of mccBsu products in wild-type and
ΔspeDB. subtilis genetic background. (C) Scheme of the B. subtilis peptidyl-adenylate aminopropylation pathway. R stands for the N-terminal part
of MccABsu, MKVKKIKKKKPIKIGFDGPVM.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. (A) Structure of the E. coli AspRS/tRNAAsp complex with the natural substrate aspartyl-adenylate (PDB: 1c0a) and with superimposed
tandem-aminopropylated isoasparagine-adenylate docked into the enzyme active center using the CB-Dock2 homologous template fitting server
and further refined with the docking package of Molsoft ICM-Pro. The protein is shown in gray ribbons, the aspartyl-adenylate and tandem-
aminopropylated isoasparagine-adenylate are shown as thick CPK-colored sticks, and the carbon atoms are in pink and yellow, respectively. The
tRNA is removed for clarity. The insets in panels B and C are the zoom-in views of a selected area in AspRS, showing the contacts of the ligands
with the residues of the substrate-binding pocket (thin CPK-colored sticks, except that carbon atoms are in beige) located at interacting distances of
<3.5 Å. Dashed lines indicate likely polar (blue) and hydrophobic (yellow) interactions. (D) Tandem aminopropylation increases the bioactivity of
E. coli McC. Minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of E. coli McC antibiotics without secondary modification (Eco-McC) and with a single (Eco-
McCap) and tandem aminopropyl groups (Eco-McCapap). MIC of the compound is defined as a minimal concentration at which a growth inhibition
zone is visible in a drop diffusion assay.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. McCBsu production changes the social behavior of B. subtilis.
(A) Expression of mccBsu BGC prevents biofilm formation in
heterologous hosts. B. subtilis 3A38 strain harboring either an
empty pHT01 vector or pHT01 expressing indicated mccBsu genes
were grown on the biofilm-inducing modified LB agar supplemented
with IPTG for 24 h. (B) Inactivation of Bsu-McC production renders
the native producer B. subtilis MG27 strain biofilm-proficient. B.
subtilis MG27 w.t., ΔspeD mutant, and mccBBsu null mutant
(mccBΩloxP) were grown on modified LB agar for 24 h. The B.
subtilis MG27 ΔspeD mutant was used as a biofilm-negative control.
Strains used in the biofilm-formation tests produced either no Bsu-
McC (″Bsu-McC−″), adenylated peptide only (″Bsu-McC*+″), or
tandem−aminopropylated microcin C (″Bsu-McC+″).
